facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old man
recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of his right thumb
four-year history of a lesion at that site
partial amputation of the thumb was performed in December 2016
the lesion reappeared at the distal aspect of the thumb stump
no significant medical history
took no medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, indurated lesion
no palpable lymphadenopathy was noted
enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease
